To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the novel mini-DOAS spectrometer is capable of measuring trace gas concentrations from the HALO research aircraft in all sky conditions, even under clouds and fog, and that the uncertainties of the retrieved trace gas concentrations from our scaling method can be estimated with sufficient precision for most of the trace gases of interest.

the novel mini-DOAS limb instrument is able to infer the mixing ratio of trace gases with absorption cross sections in the UV and visible spectral ranges from measurements of their limb absorption spectra under all types of atmospheric conditions, including clouds.

we report on the first airborne mini-DOAS measurements of NO2, BrO, O4, O2-O2 and H2O in limb geometry, and that we report on first measurements of the NO2 and BrONO2 vertical profiles from the HALO research aircraft in the Antarctic region.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development, testing, and validation of the new mini-DOAS spectrometer for airborne limb measurements of UV/vis trace gases, aerosol and cloud particles, and radiance measurements in the UV/Vis and NIR spectral regions.

the development and testing of a new instrument for airborne measurements of UV/vis trace gases in the troposphere and lowermost stratosphere, and the development and testing a novel method to infer the trace gas mixing ratios from the absorption measurements.
the development of the mini-DOAS spectrometer and the scaling method for airborne UV / vis limb spectroscopy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this novel airborne instrument is a very powerful tool to measure trace gases and aerosol particles in the atmosphere under all sky conditions.
the scaling method works well in the case of a strong absorber (e.g., NO2) under all sky conditions.
this novel instrument is capable of inferring trace gas mixing ratios from UV/vis limb spectroscopy with a precision of about 10% and an accuracy of about 20% under all sky conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel miniaturized UV/vis spectrometer, which is able to measure the atmospheric trace gases NO2 and Br2O from the aircraft altitude of 10-13 km with an accuracy better than 10% and 20%, respectively, under all sky conditions.
we have developed and successfully tested a novel instrument for the airborne measurement of trace gases and aerosols in the UV/visible and near-infrared spectral regions.

the novel HALO miniDOAS instrument is capable of inferring trace gas mixing ratios of NO2 and O4 in the troposphere and lower stratosphere with an accuracy of 10% and a precision of a few percent, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mini-DOAS is a versatile instrument that can be used to measure a large variety of atmospheric trace gases and aerosol species, which are of relevance for atmospheric chemistry, climate, and the Earth's radiative energy balance, from aboard an aircraft in a wide range of atmospheric conditions.
the mini-DOAS is a powerful instrument for the simultaneous measurement of a variety of atmospheric trace gases and aerosols from the aircraft in all weather conditions.
the scaling method is a viable and powerful tool for the analysis of mini-DOAS limb measurements of UV/vis trace gases under all skies and at all altitudes.
